the porcine pCLCA4 gene mirrors the human ortholog hCLCA4 in its genomic structure and cellular processing and that pCLCA4 is strongly expressed in the lung of pigs, but not in the mouse.
we characterized the porcine hCLCA4 ortholog, pCLCA6a, and found it expressed in the pig lung, whereas its murine orthologue is not expressed in mouse lungs.
the genomic structure, the protein processing, and the tissue expression pattern of the porcines chloride channel calcium-activated family member pCLCA4A mirror that of the human hCLCA4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new member of the chloride channel calcium-activated (CLCA) family of proteins in pigs, the porcine pCLCA4.
the characterization of the pCLCA family of genes and proteins, which are expressed in a species-specific fashion.
a better understanding of the porcines CLCA4 gene and its protein product, pCLCA-4a.

the porcine CLCA4a protein is expressed in porcines and humans but not in mice, and this may be one of the reasons for the different CF phenotypes in these species.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pig CLCA4a protein is the first CLCA family member found in the lung of a nonhuman species.
the pig is a better model to study hCLCA4 than the mouse is.
the porcine CLCA4a gene is a close ortholog of human CLCA4 and is strongly expressed in the porcine lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the porcine CLCA member pCLCA4 is a good model for the human CLCA member hCLCA, and it can be used as a model to study the role and regulation of hCLCA in CF.
the porcine pCLCA4 ortholog of hCLCA is expressed in the lung, whereas the murine ortholog is not.
